evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: graphic forms, formation account, early uses, and readings
evidence.text: The entry lists one small-seal form, five bronze examples (three displayed), and three bamboo/slip examples; it displays no oracle-bone example. Its analysis says the bronze graph combines 刀 and 珏, interpreted as a knife dividing jade, with ‘cut/split jade’ extended to ‘separate.’ It reports early bronze and Chu-slip uses as personal names, including 毛班. Those name contexts do not establish the proposed ‘split jade’ sense. The entry gives Mandarin bān and Guangyun fanqie 布還.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 班

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: formation, graphic change, readings, and recorded senses
evidence.text: The entry transcribes the Shuowen gloss 分瑞玉 and analyzes the seal form as 玨 plus 刀. It describes a stroke and dot in the regular-script form as a changed form of 刀, without dating that graphic change. It gives Mandarin bān and records examples glossed as distributing jade tokens, separating, promulgating, equality, rank/order, scheduled transport, work shifts, and groups. These dictionary examples do not establish a linear chronology or semantic links.
evidence.title: 班 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, transcription and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The page transcribes 班 as 分瑞玉。从𤤴从刀. Duan Yucai classifies the analysis as 會意, explaining that a knife divides, and notes an association between 班 and 頒 in the sense of distribution. This is a historical lexicographic explanation, not an inscriptional gloss contemporary with the cited bronze name uses.
evidence.title: 說文解字「班」

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The 斑 entry distinguishes its graphic account from 班’s traditional 玨-and-刀 analysis. The different graphic analyses do not establish that 斑 developed graphically from 班 or that the two words are cognate.
evidence.title: 斑 — Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

gaps: The local rows supplied for this task give Unihan kMandarin dāo for 刀 and 刂, jué for 玨, bān for 班 and 斑. The local file is sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt. Direct official per-character Unihan pages could not be verified, so these local rows are not emitted as external evidence.

The local Baxter–Sagart table gives 班 MC paen, OC *pˤ<r>an; 斑 MC paen, OC *pˤran; 玨 MC kaewk, OC *[k]ˤrok; and 刀 MC taw, OC *C.tˤaw. The table is sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv. The upstream reconstruction PDF failed to open, so the local readings are reported here as a dataset cross-check, not external evidence. In particular, do not silently substitute 斑’s *pˤran for 班’s *pˤ<r>an.

No evidence in the inspected sources establishes 刀 or 玨 as a phonetic component in 班. No sound-loan account was found; the knife’s independent ancient name or pronunciation is not established by reconstructing 班.

The Commons description page and exact image URL for 班-seal.svg were inaccessible. The MediaWiki imageinfo API was also attempted and inaccessible. The local SVG could not be rendered by the available image viewer. Its literal identity, provenance, dating scope, and license therefore remain unverified; do not select it or describe its pixels as inspected.

The earliest cited bronze contexts are personal names. The secure earliest lexical use for ‘divide/distribute’ remains unresolved; the received-text citations do not establish composition dates. The database entry’s lack of an oracle-bone example is a coverage limit, not proof that none exists.

The CUHK database and the Shuowen explanation support reporting the knife-and-paired-jade analysis as a traditional interpretation. The reviewed evidence does not independently prove the depicted action from an inspected early glyph image. The dictionary sense lists do not establish the chronology or semantic links among separation, distribution, equality, rank, and group meanings.
The broader Proto-Sino-Tibetan, Austroasiatic, and proposed 班/斑/羆 comparisons in the dossier were not checked against their underlying publications in this bounded search.
